answer: Because the kernel audit recomputes usage from the gale history, a padded declaration is a losing trade rather than a cheap one. A farm running 49 keys therefore forfeits for 49 separate budgets, and each of them has to be real to survive a spot-check of the ripple declaration. Each identity declares a compute budget of 279 units per epoch and the declaration is bound to its signing key, so two identities cannot share one budget without a visible collision. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
